questions.q: What did early thinkers like Maharishi Kanad propose about matter?
questions.a: That matter can be divided again and only until a stage comes beyond which further division is not possible - the smallest particle (parmanu).

questions.q: What did Dalton add to the idea of atoms?
questions.a: He made it scientific: all matter is made of tiny indivisible atoms that combine in small whole-number ratios to form compounds.

questions.q: Why were atoms considered indivisible later proved wrong?
questions.a: Experiments (like cathode rays) showed atoms contain smaller charged particles - electrons, protons and neutrons.

concepts.title: Thomson's Atomic Model and Cathode Rays

questions.q: Describe Thomson's model of the atom.
questions.a: A sphere of positive charge with electrons embedded in it like seeds in a watermelon - total charge zero.

questions.q: What observation does Thomson's model explain?
questions.a: The atom is electrically neutral - equal positive and negative charges balance.

questions.q: Why was Thomson's model eventually rejected?
questions.a: Rutherford's gold foil experiment showed most of the atom is empty with a tiny dense positive nucleus, not uniform positive charge.

questions.q: State Bohr's key postulate about electron orbits.
questions.a: Electrons revolve only in certain allowed orbits (shells) with fixed energy and do not radiate energy while in them.

questions.q: How are shells named?
questions.a: K, L, M, N... outward from the nucleus, each holding at most 2n squared electrons.

questions.q: Why do electrons in Bohr's orbits not fall into the nucleus?
questions.a: Each allowed orbit has a definite energy; electrons in these stationary states do not lose energy by radiating.

questions.q: What is the atomic number of an element?
questions.a: The number of protons in its nucleus - the same as the number of electrons in a neutral atom.

questions.q: Why is atomic number the true identity of an element?
questions.a: Every atom of an element has the same proton number, and no two elements share it.

questions.q: An atom has 12 protons. What element is it and how many electrons has it?
questions.a: Magnesium (atomic number 12); a neutral atom has 12 electrons.

What are isotopes?
questions.a: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers (different neutrons).

questions.q: Give one medical and one industrial use of isotopes.
questions.a: Cobalt-60 or iodine-131 treat cancer and thyroid disorders; uranium-235 is fuel in nuclear reactors.

questions.q: Why do isotopes of an element show the same chemical properties?
questions.a: Chemical behaviour depends on electron count, which is the same since the atomic number is the same.

What are isobars?
questions.a: Atoms of different elements with different atomic numbers but the same mass number.

questions.q: Give an example of isobars.
questions.a: Calcium-40 (20 protons) and argon-40 (18 protons) - both mass number 40.

questions.q: How do isobars differ chemically?
questions.a: They are different elements with different electron counts, so their chemical properties differ.
